svg.title: Complex cutoffs and the exact adjoint pairing
svg.desc: On an interval J contained in (3,4), choose the complex cutoff theta equal to i. Then B equals t times differentiation, its true adjoint is minus t times differentiation minus one, and omitting conjugation produces the opposite operator. For a nonzero real smooth function chi with compact support in J and a tangential function phi of L2 norm one, the correct pairings both equal minus one half of the integral of chi squared, while the unconjugated formula gives plus one half. This is the witness proved in CC1 through CC3, not a numerical approximation.

g.text: Conjugating the cutoff fixes the adjoint pairing
Exact witness from Example 8.3 and the complex-cutoff correction (CC1)–(CC3)
Choose θ = θ₀ + iη, with θ₀ = 1 on [−1,2] and θ = i on J ⊂ (3,4).
Test u = v = φ(x′)χ(t), with χ ∈ C∞c(J) real and nonzero, and ‖φ‖₂ = 1.
Dₜ t θ̅, including the derivative of t
Integration by parts: ∫ tχ′χ dt = −½ ∫ χ² dt. Both endpoints vanish by compact support.
The original global boundary term also vanishes: the factor t kills t = 0; θ kills the far tail.
Inner product linear in its first variable. For n = 1, omit φ and use measure one on ℝ⁰. Original figure: CC0.
